recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Only revisit Communication element ordering if Patient Care opens a new issue that intentionally supersedes the later workflow-alignment sequencing.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive DSTU2 Patient Care QA issue reporting that Communication elements were out of order and expecting Communication.recipient to appear before topic/context/sent/received/sender/reason.
initial_application: Git commit 047a0c6ab1c00e633177a675d7146fc48793bf00 applied FHIR-12681 by moving Communication.recipient earlier in the then-authoritative Communication spreadsheet and reordering affected Communication examples.
additional_context: Communication is active in source/fhir.ini, but the old spreadsheet source was retired when the resource moved to StructureDefinition XML. Later Published issue FHIR-14446 changed Communication.recipient semantics from who.focus to who.actor/Event.performer.actor, and implementation commit 0b3156fcf0c2c6f49163a515ab17173a52cc8deb explicitly says that mapping change triggered element re-sequencing. The current StructureDefinition XML preserves that later ordering and current examples align with it. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-12681 found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because restoring the original DSTU2 recipient-before-topic ordering would conflict with a later applied workflow-alignment decision.
